mcqs.learning_point: Understand qualitative statement of second law
mcqs.question: Which of the following pairs correctly compares the Kelvin‑Planck and Clausius statements of the second law?

options.A: Kelvin‑Planck: It is impossible to construct a device that operates in a cycle and produces no effect other than the absorption of heat from a single reservoir and the performance of an equivalent amount of work. Clausius: Heat cannot spontaneously flow from a colder body to a hotter body.
options.B: Kelvin‑Planck: Heat cannot spontaneously flow from a colder body to a hotter body. Clausius: It is impossible to construct a device that operates in a cycle and produces no effect other than the absorption of heat from a single reservoir and the performance of an equivalent amount of work.
options.C: Kelvin‑Planck: All processes increase entropy. Clausius: Entropy of an isolated system remains constant.
options.D: Kelvin‑Planck: Work can be completely converted into heat without any loss. Clausius: Heat can be completely converted into work without any loss.

mcqs.answer: Kelvin‑Planck: It is impossible to construct a device that operates in a cycle and produces no effect other than the absorption of heat from a single reservoir and the performance of an equivalent amount of work. Clausius: Heat cannot spontaneously flow from a colder body to a hotter body.
mcqs.explanation: Option A states the standard Kelvin‑Planck statement (no cyclic device can convert heat from a single reservoir entirely into work) and the Clausius statement (heat cannot flow spontaneously from cold to hot). Both are the correct qualitative forms of the second law. The other options either swap the statements, give incorrect entropy descriptions, or claim impossible complete conversions, which contradict the second law.

mcqs.question: Two isolated bodies, A at 300 K and B at 500 K, are placed in thermal contact. According to the second law of thermodynamics, which statement is correct about the spontaneous heat flow?

options.A: Heat will flow spontaneously from body A to body B.
options.B: Heat will flow spontaneously from body B to body A.
options.C: No net heat flow will occur because the system is isolated.
options.D: The direction of heat flow depends on the pressure of the bodies.

mcqs.answer: Heat will flow spontaneously from body B to body A.
mcqs.explanation: The second law (Clausius statement) dictates that heat flows spontaneously from a higher temperature to a lower temperature. Hence, heat moves from the hotter body B (500 K) to the colder body A (300 K). Option A reverses the direction, C ignores the temperature difference, and D introduces an irrelevant factor.

mcqs.question: A heat engine operates between a hot reservoir at 600 K and a cold reservoir at 300 K. What is the maximum possible efficiency of this engine according to the second law?
mcqs.explanation: The Carnot (maximum) efficiency is η_max = 1 – T_c/T_h = 1 – 300/600 = 0.5, i.e., 50 %. This is the theoretical upper limit; real engines have lower efficiencies. Options B, C, and D are inconsistent with the Carnot formula.

mcqs.learning_point: Distinguish reversible and irreversible processes at the required level
mcqs.question: Which of the following processes is reversible?

options.A: Free expansion of an ideal gas into a vacuum.
options.B: Quasistatic isothermal expansion of an ideal gas with an infinitesimal pressure difference between the system and surroundings.
options.C: Spontaneous mixing of two different gases.
options.D: Spontaneous heat flow from a hot body to a cold body.

mcqs.answer: Quasistatic isothermal expansion of an ideal gas with an infinitesimal pressure difference between the system and surroundings.
mcqs.explanation: A reversible process must be infinitesimally close to equilibrium at every stage, allowing the system to be returned to its initial state without net changes elsewhere. Option B meets this criterion. Options A, C, and D are inherently irreversible because they involve spontaneous, non‑equilibrium changes.

mcqs.learning_point: Understand qualitative statement of second law
mcqs.question: The second law of thermodynamics can be stated qualitatively as:

options.A: Energy cannot be created or destroyed.
options.B: The entropy of an isolated system never decreases.
options.C: Heat can be completely converted into work.
options.D: The total energy of the universe remains constant.

mcqs.answer: The entropy of an isolated system never decreases.
mcqs.explanation: Option B captures the qualitative essence of the second law: entropy of an isolated system either increases or remains constant (for reversible processes). Option A describes the first law, while C and D are incorrect statements about energy conversion and conservation.

mcqs.question: A metal rod has one end at 350 K and the other end at 300 K. When the ends are left free, heat will flow:

options.A: From the colder end to the hotter end.
options.B: From the hotter end to the colder end.
options.C: No net heat flow will occur.

mcqs.answer: From the hotter end to the colder end.
mcqs.explanation: According to the second law (Clausius statement), heat spontaneously flows from higher to lower temperature. Therefore, heat moves from the 350 K end toward the 300 K end. Options A, C, and D contradict this principle.

mcqs.question: A Carnot engine operates between a hot reservoir at 400 K and a cold reservoir at 300 K. Which statement about its performance is correct?

options.A: Its efficiency can exceed 50% if friction is minimized.
options.C: It can convert all absorbed heat into work.
options.D: Its efficiency is independent of the temperatures of the reservoirs.

mcqs.explanation: The Carnot efficiency is η = 1 – T_c/T_h = 1 – 300/400 = 0.25 (25 %). This is the maximum possible efficiency for any engine between those temperatures. Options A and C violate the second law, and D is false because efficiency depends on the temperature difference.

mcqs.learning_point: Distinguish reversible and irreversible processes at the required level
mcqs.question: A gas expands rapidly against a piston with a constant external pressure that is slightly less than the internal pressure, and the expansion occurs with noticeable friction. Which description best fits this process?
mcqs.explanation: The rapid, non‑quasistatic expansion with friction makes the process irreversible. Since no heat exchange is mentioned, it is treated as adiabatic. Hence option B correctly characterises the process. Options A and C assume reversibility, and D assumes the temperature remains constant, which is not guaranteed without heat exchange.
